capabilities.notes: Packages and instances are persisted as one atomic catalog; legacy mutable package payloads are copied into canonical SHA-256 revision paths, APK/native paths reject managed symlink traversal, stale revisions and orphan instance directories are swept, and post-commit cleanup failures are surfaced as maintenance warnings. Filesystem crash durability remains device-deferred.

Package and instance mutations are serialized in a dedicated :sandbox_package service. Only the AMS-recorded host main process can mint a PID/UID-bound Binder capability; client death and per-call caller checks revoke or reject reuse. Real Binder/AMS behavior remains device-deferred, and shared-UID containment is not a malicious-code security boundary.
Package metadata and virtual policy are issued by the Binder-owned package authority and revision-bound into runtime requests; Android Binder behavior remains not-tested.
Permission overrides are isolated by package and virtual user and are atomically persisted; host manifest/runtime permission enforcement and device behavior remain outside current evidence.
Simple AppOps integer and boolean decisions are supplied from the virtual package snapshot; complex return surfaces and Android service behavior remain not-tested.

Generation recovery and same-revision reuse are source-wired. APK SHA-256 is verified in Broker and Guest; a different revision invalidates all live processes for the virtual instance. Android process/cache behavior remains device-deferred.

Explicit manifest Receiver routing and deterministic on-demand Guest process activation are wired; implicit resolution is tracked separately, while platform background/protected-broadcast behavior remains device-deferred.

Broker action index, action/category/data/MIME matching, stable priority ordering, dual permission checks and on-demand process delivery are locally wired; Android platform implicit-broadcast restrictions remain device-deferred.

Priority-ordered result propagation, abort/clear-abort, bounded chain-wide execution budget, per-receiver timeout accounting, skipped/terminal statistics, failure policy and payload limits are wired at Broker/Guest source level. Android platform background-delivery and OEM behavior remain device-unverified.

Broker one-shot token authority, sync/async PendingResult capture, finishReceiver interception, Binder-death cancellation, bounded payload validation, deadline cleanup, Session cancellation, replay and late-token rejection are source-wired. Hidden-API and API/OEM execution remain device-unverified.

Dynamic registrations, Manifest indexes/bindings, Action Index/start templates and Ordered completion tokens share one lifecycle coordinator and one runtime-status snapshot. Session recovery, disconnect, stop, instance invalidation, Broker destroy and token expiry are source-wired; real Android broadcast lifecycle remains device-deferred.
Session/generation-bound TTL, one-time atomic consumption, revoke and lifecycle cleanup are locally verified; Android platform URI-permission behavior remains device-deferred.
Broker-owned callback registration and URI matching are locally verified; Android ContentResolver/IContentObserver behavior remains device-deferred.
Bounded Broker/Guest batch routing is locally verified; Android ContentResolver, Binder and third-party Provider transaction behavior remain device-deferred.

A dedicated Service-only isolated transport is production-wired through four predeclared android:isolatedProcess workers, an independent SessionRegistry, per-generation capability tokens, typed outer identity, platform PID/UID evidence and Binder-death recovery. Non-Service isolated components fail closed. Real APK/data-root accessibility, platform UID/SELinux behavior and Android AMS lifecycle remain blocked on the unavailable locked Android build/device environment.

Guest application bootstrap is source-wired with host-internal class denial and principal Context storage redirection. Same-UID hostile-code isolation and Android framework behavior remain outside this evidence level.
Guest native-library PLT/GOT file calls are policy-bound and fail-closed; Android linker, SELinux, kernel race behavior, simulator and device execution remain not-tested.

Guest modules route socket creation/close, bind/connect, sendto/recvfrom, local/peer address queries, sensitive socket options, DNS, hostname and interface identity through a bounded fail-closed native network policy. Virtual Connectivity metadata includes network ID, transport, VPN, metering, validation, MTU, proxy and private DNS. Android VPN/ConnectivityService and OEM behavior remain device-deferred.

dlopen/android_dlopen_ext now enforce Guest-root resolution, ELF class/machine/type matching, library-FD offsets, bounded extension flags, RELRO descriptor policy, reserved-address alignment and foreign-namespace denial with audit status. Bionic/API linker behavior and actual APK RELRO remain device-deferred.

Runtime diagnostics record bounded Java crash evidence, ANR episode start/continuation/recovery with thread dumps, rotated exports and SHA-256 manifests. Native fatal-signal capture uses an alternate signal stack and records PID/TID/signal/code/address/session/generation/process/ABI; the host test executes a real SIGSEGV child fixture. Android tombstone/DropBox/AMS ANR correlation remains device-deferred.

Persisted Binder-owned staged sessions support multi-select import, seal/retry/abandon, bounded artifact copying and stale cleanup. Android document-provider grants and process-death behavior remain untested.
Base, feature and configuration split metadata is validated and dependency ordered. Full Android PackageInstaller parity and every manifest edge case are not claimed.
Every APK artifact has an immutable digest and the package revision is a deterministic set digest; Binder and Guest verify the complete set before use.
Dependency-ordered split APK paths feed class loading, resources, ApplicationInfo and createContextForSplit. ART and AssetManager behavior still requires Android validation.
uses-library names are retained in package and runtime metadata. Library resolution, required/optional semantics, native shared-library namespaces and device availability checks are not implemented.

Runtime-permission requests and audit introduced in Catalog v4 remain atomically persisted in current schema v5 alongside per-user package/component state. Android process-death and filesystem behavior remain untested.
A typed PID/UID-bound capability is issued only to the recorded Runtime Broker process and is closed on client Binder death. Shared-UID hostile-code resistance is not claimed.

Host Activity permission callbacks are resolved through Runtime Broker and Package Service before an effective result is delivered to the Guest Activity. Real Android callback/token behavior is untested.

Dangerous permissions are effective only when both the virtual decision and the system-owned host package capability allow them. Runtime permission groups, one-time grants and OEM policy behavior remain untested.

The active Guest generation replaces permission and AppOps state without restart. M4-T9 actively releases tracked Location callbacks and Camera device handles when policy is revoked; native/static APIs and unrecognized resources remain outside this bounded cleanup model.
Typed Binder snapshots carry filter priority, actions, categories, scheme/host/path rules and MIME declarations from the trusted package revision into the active Guest generation.

Guest-local Activity, Service and Receiver resolution applies action/category/data/MIME rules, deterministic priority/specificity ordering, explicit package/component isolation and MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY. Exact Android IntentFilter parity remains device-gated.
Per-virtual-user package and declared-component enabled overrides persist in Catalog v5, are writable only through the management capability and affect package availability and component visibility.

First-install time survives upgrades, last-update time advances, a stable virtual installer identity is exposed, component PackageInfo flags are honored and declared shared-library names remain in the revision snapshot.

Explicit Guest package/component queries fail closed on local no-match or disabled state, host identity remains hidden, and non-Guest implicit/system queries retain the bounded host fallback. Full cross-package merged listings are not implemented.

Camera, Location and bounded AudioManager Binder methods are gated by effective virtual permission plus AppOps. An effectively granted capability fails closed when its reflective proxy is unavailable. Native AudioRecord/MediaRecorder and static/native APIs are not covered.

Tracked Location callbacks and returned Camera device handles are released best-effort when same-generation permission/AppOps policy is revoked or the Guest session closes. Android/OEM service signatures remain device-gated.

Each Guest generation keeps a bounded in-memory audit of allowed, denied, failed and cleanup capability events and exposes counts plus compact records through runtime status. It is diagnostic evidence, not persistent security logging.

Known integer AppOps codes, proxy operations and nested AttributionSource identity chains use virtual policy; attribution tags are preserved and unknown integer operations fail closed to MODE_DEFAULT.

Runtime permission request/report validation and Package Service delegation are extracted from RuntimeBrokerService behind a testable gateway and session resolver. Other Broker responsibilities remain large and require further decomposition.

Revision-scoped Alarm records persist exact/allow-while-idle/repeating state and Listener or durable PendingIntent delivery identity in Package Service. Offline Guest processes retain schedules; a new generation reclaims and delivers by persistent PendingIntent token. Android wakeup, Doze, reboot and OEM timing behavior remain device-gated.

Clipboard contents are Binder-owned and shared across Guest processes of one package/virtual user while remaining isolated from other virtual users and the host clipboard. Real Android ClipData/OEM listener behavior remains unverified.

Basic accounts, passwords and auth tokens are persisted by package and virtual user and shared across Guest processes through a scoped Binder capability. Authenticator/OAuth UI and full AccountManager asynchronous protocol remain unsupported.

Notification IDs/tags, channel/group lifecycle, foreground-service mapping and click/delete/action PendingIntent identities are revision-scoped and persistent. Group/channel deletion cascades only through owned resources and cancelAll enumerates owned host IDs. OEM listener callbacks and real process/device restoration remain unverified.
Job IDs use a persistent package/user/revision namespace shared across Guest processes. Query and cancel operations retain Guest IDs while the host receives only owned rewritten IDs.
Typed AIDL exposes a Runtime-Broker-only scoped capability for clipboard, account, alarm and persistent namespace operations without Bundle business payloads.
Package Service owns durable per-package/per-user system-service state, death-linked capability sessions, process/generation-owned alarms and best-effort cleanup after instance deletion.
Runtime Broker obtains a package/user/process/generation-scoped Binder capability and injects it into the Guest spec; capability lifetime follows the Runtime session.
Guest framework state delegates to a remote authority so Clipboard, Account and namespace state is shared across Guest processes without exposing the Package Service root Binder.
Notification and Job guest-to-host ID mappings persist by package and virtual user across Guest process restarts. Full notification/job object lifecycle remains separately partial.
Typed Notification/Channel/Job lifecycle records and synchronous Job callback acknowledgement are exposed through the scoped virtual system-service capability.
Active Notification records and Channel/Group metadata persist by package/user; cancelAll enumerates and cancels only owned host IDs without invoking host-global cancelAll.
Typed Guest JobInfo ownership, constraints, timing, retry counters, stable host ID and process/generation/revision state survive Package Service recreation; stale revisions are pruned.
Trusted Host JobService dispatches to the owning Guest JobService; synchronous acceptance, scoped asynchronous jobFinished, stop and reschedule decisions are wired through typed capabilities.
Provider cursor/file close delivery and cross-registry cleanup orchestration are extracted from RuntimeBrokerService into a dedicated coordinator.
Version-neutral bounded JobParameters data and one-shot execution/host callback capabilities replace direct host callback exposure and Bundle transport.
Persistent Job state now transitions SCHEDULED→DISPATCHING→RUNNING with owner process/generation validation, binder death handling, timeout reschedule and stale capability invalidation.
Guest runtime resolves and creates the declared JobService, reconstructs bounded JobParameters and invokes onStartJob/onStopJob on the Guest main thread.

A scoped one-shot execution Binder maps Guest JobService.jobFinished to the trusted Host JobService callback; old generations, completed capabilities and mismatched job IDs cannot finish current work.
Started, bound, foreground, recovery and connection-lease orchestration are extracted from RuntimeBrokerService into a dedicated Service coordinator.
Bound-service client tokens are linked to Binder death; dead clients are removed from Broker ownership and receive best-effort Guest onUnbind delivery.
START_STICKY and START_REDELIVER_INTENT ownership survives Guest process death; recovery recreates the Service in the new Generation and redelivers the latest bounded action when required.

startForegroundService pending-promotion state, bounded deadline, background-start allow/exemption policy, declared/requested type validation, notification ownership, demotion, process-death recovery and timeout cleanup are wired in Broker and Guest source paths. SystemUI/AMS/OEM enforcement remains device-unverified.
Virtual task policy now applies bounded Android-compatible NO_HISTORY, FORWARD_RESULT, EXCLUDE_FROM_RECENTS, RETAIN_IN_RECENTS, NEW_DOCUMENT, CLEAR_TOP, REORDER_TO_FRONT and launch-mode interactions.
FLAG_ACTIVITY_FORWARD_RESULT transfers the one-shot result owner from the intermediate Activity to the terminal callee and rejects invalid or ownerless forwarding.
Broker-owned task/back-stack and saved-state metadata persist atomically with CRC validation; corrupt state is quarantined and route-bound deliveries are dropped fail-closed on restore.
Typed, versioned AIDL request/result/task projections expose bounded running/recent task queries and owner-checked move-to-front/remove-task mutations scoped to the active Session and generation.
Running tasks are returned front-first; bounded recent history respects EXCLUDE_FROM_RECENTS and retained document-task policy and remains isolated by package and virtual user.

Guest ActivityManager/ActivityTaskManager running, recent and app-task queries are projected from Broker-owned virtual tasks. Task move/remove/finish operations bind framework Activity tokens to virtual Task identity and fail closed without host task-result fallback.
Typed Bundle-free Alarm and Notification records carry revision, scheduling, PendingIntent and foreground-service metadata across the scoped Binder capability.

Package Service retains one-shot and repeating alarms while the Guest is offline, rebinds generation ownership, retries unavailable targets and dispatches recovered PendingIntent alarms by durable token.

Owned notification state persists content/delete/action PendingIntent references and foreground-service keys; PendingIntent cancellation clears matching references and channel/group deletion cascades through owned state.
Bundle-free typed Job policy carries network, charging, battery, storage, idle, periodic, latency, deadline, expedited, persisted and backoff state across the scoped Binder capability.

JobScheduler schedule/enqueue extracts Android JobInfo policy into virtual typed state before host ID/service rewriting; pending JobInfo objects retain their original constraints while IDs are projected back to Guest values.

Package Service persists periodic scheduling, minimum latency, override deadline, linear/exponential bounded backoff, failure count, next-run time and APK revision cleanup; stale RUNNING/DISPATCHING work recovers to SCHEDULED.

Guest-library PLT/GOT hooks apply confinement policy to openat2, statx, renameat2, faccessat2, getdents64 and file-backed mmap. Host-native tests execute each path; Android API/ABI behavior remains device-deferred.
/proc/self/maps, cmdline and status are materialized as bounded read-only Guest snapshots. Host private mappings are redacted and PID/UID/process identity is virtualized.

dlopen and android_dlopen_ext are routed through Guest native-root and explicit system-soname policy. Unknown sonames, Host private paths and foreign linker namespaces fail closed; real Android linker namespace behavior remains device-deferred.

Guest native socket creation, IPv4/IPv6 connect, DNS/reverse-DNS, hostname, uname and interface enumeration are routed through fail-closed policy. Interface and host identity are projected from a bounded typed NativeNetworkIdentity; Android VPN/Connectivity OEM behavior remains device-deferred.

RECORD_AUDIO/AppOps policy configures a generation-bound native capture gate. AAudio and NDK MediaRecorder start/stop symbols are intercepted when imported; permission revocation invalidates active native tokens, best-effort stops tracked handles and existing Binder audio leases are cleaned up.

Bundle-free signature-permission Binder contracts carry protocol, session, generation, virtual user, package revision, single-use nonce, requested 32-bit ABI, operation and bounded artifact metadata. The companion validates protocol, nonce replay, bitness, ABI, generation identity, path containment, byte count and SHA-256 before accepting execution artifacts.

Source/build configuration separates arm64-v8a/x86_64 Host libraries from armeabi-v7a/x86 companion libraries and compiles an independent controlled_sandbox_native32 target. Android APK packaging and installation are not proven in this source-only stage.

64-bit ABIs route to the Host Runtime Broker. armeabi-v7a/x86 guests are staged through a signature-protected bounded file channel and route prepare, Activity, Service, Receiver, Provider and stop operations to the production Runtime Broker embedded in the 32-bit Companion. Unknown or legacy ABI metadata fails closed. Android packaging and device execution remain untested.

M4-T18 freezes the exact legacy Bundle AIDL exception set, rejects new unapproved Bundle business contracts, enforces production source-size thresholds and keeps persistence/task decomposition under an executable source gate.

A machine-readable audit covers bounded state, rollback, identity ownership, Binder/process death cleanup, revision cleanup and Guest-query Host-fallback controls across twelve resource domains and three query surfaces.

The repository is source-ready for the next device-test stage, with unresolved production and device tracks recorded explicitly. This status does not claim an Android build, Emulator run, third-party APK compatibility or stability evidence.
